correctness.rationale: The source arXiv:2302.14664v1, Corollary 11 and Theorem 13, supplies only nonequivariant concentration in degree 2. Separating pure star/top cliques from mixed two-rank faces produces formula (5); mixed faces have a unique endpoint on one rank and a double-count only for edges. The incidence graph is connected and its chain class is computed independently. Jacobi–Trudi telescoping gives precisely the three- and four-row Specht sums. Semisimplicity yields the actual rational representation, and subgroup invariants give quotient rational acyclicity. Exact independent signed Lefschetz computations pass all conjugacy classes for six (m,k) pairs, including two size-8 cases; the proof, not those experiments, covers all parameters.

value.rationale: The adjacent-rank complex has a nontrivial incidence-graph cycle representation not determined by Betti counts or by the individual-rank equivariant theorems. The complete rational S_m decomposition is uniform for all m>=5 and 2<=k<=m-3 and reveals the three-row irreducible series, distinct from both four-row pure-rank series. It also resolves the rational quotient homology under S_m and A_m; the invariant is a natural missing equivariant refinement of an explicitly studied infinite family.
